item.title: Is the US actually too chicken to take on China for trade?
item.description: A weak yuan guarantees Beijing massive trade surplus even as the White House tries tamp down on Chinese imports Since China offered a truce in the trade war last October following its threat to deprive the United States of rare-earth magnets, the Trump administration has been happy to stop escalating. After all, imports from China have been falling, down by 40% in the year to June, compared with the same period in 2024. Best to declare victory and call it a day. item.title: 1958, the US secretly detonated 3 nuclear devices 100–500 km above the South Atlantic
item.description: In a clandestine effort, Operation Argus conducted nuclear tests in the stratosphere over the South Atlantic Ocean. These detonations resulted in spectacular artificial auroras and fleeting radiation belts around our planet. The mission’s intent was to shield against Soviet missile threats and radar detection systems. Yet, the swift vanishing of these barriers caused significant communication disturbances, leading to the formulation of international accords banning nuclear experiments in space. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Forecast energy price cap rise in Britain could push UK fuel bills up 4% this winter
item.description: Expected quarterly rise highest in three years and likely to wipe out Burnham’s VAT cut on electricity bills Household energy bills across Great Britain are expected to climb to a three-year high this winter as the impact of the Middle East war wipes out Andy Burnham’s tax cut on electricity bills. The government’s cap on energy prices is on track to rise by 4% from this October to the equivalent of £1,729 a year through the last three months of 2026, which could hit struggling households especially hard this winter, according to analysis by the energy consultancy Cornwall Insight. item.title: En 1982, Reino Unido movilizó sus barcos civiles en la guerra de las Malvinas. China ha tenido la misma idea con su descomunal flota mercante
item.description: En 1982, Reino Unido necesitaba llevar una guerra hasta unas islas situadas a más de 12.000 kilómetros de casa y descubrió que su Armada no podía hacerlo sola . La solución: recurrir a decenas de cruceros, cargueros, petroleros y otros barcos civiles para transportar soldados, aviones, combustible y suministros hasta las Malvinas. Ahora, China está estudiando la operación como modelo para un problema propio: cómo convertir su descomunal flota mercante en una enorme reserva logística (y militar) disponible en caso de guerra. item.title: Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf in Iraq for talks
item.description: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led negotiations with the United States to end the Middle East war, arrived in Baghdad on Wednesday for talks. Ghalibaf will head "a high-level parliamentary delegation to discuss regional developments" and "strengthen strategic cooperation between Tehran and Baghdad," Iran's Fars news agency said. The visit comes as Iraq faces pressure from Washington to disarm powerful Iran-backed armed factions, which have built considerable political and financial clout in the country. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran, Iran. Fuente: France 24 - English.
